Indications for Pharmacotherapy
  
Guidelines vary . See NICE guidelines
Generally considered when:
BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² (or ≥ 32.5 kg/m² for ethnic minority groups) AND at least 
one weight-related comorbidity (e.g., Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, 
dyslipidaemia, sleep apnoea, or cardiovascular disease). 
•
When there is significant risk of obesity-related disease eg; CVD
•
Failed Lifestyle interventions (diet, physical activity, and behavioural 
therapy)
In combination with lifestyle modification.
Pharmacotherapy should be a chronic, long-term treatment plan to manage 
obesity as a disease.

• Gastrointestinal lipase inhibitors : Orlistat
• GLP-1  receptor agonists:  liraglutide,  semaglutide
• Dual incretin agonists (GLP-1 +  GIP receptor agonists)

• Combination therapy:  phentermine/ topiramate
